title: Chemical Reactions and Equations
subject: Science

blocks.text: A chemical reaction is a process in which one or more substances change into new substances with different properties. The substances that take part in a chemical reaction are called reactants, and the new substances formed are called products.

A chemical equation is a short representation of a chemical reaction using the symbols and chemical formulae of the substances involved.

So, remember:
Chemical Reaction = Actual process
Chemical Equation = Symbolic representation of the process

This equation is called a skeletal chemical equation because it represents the reaction but is not balanced.
Remember: Reactants are written on the left-hand side, and products are written on the right-hand side.

A balanced chemical equation is an equation in which the number of atoms of each element is equal on both sides of the equation. This is based on the Law of Conservation of Mass, which states that mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

Chemical reactions can be classified into different types depending on how the reactants change into products. The main types are:
These reactions have different patterns, which help us identify them easily.
A combination reaction is a reaction in which two or more substances combine to form a single product.
Here, two or more reactants combine to form only one product.
Calcium reacts with oxygen to form calcium oxide:
Here, calcium and oxygen combine to form one product, calcium oxide.
Hydrogen reacts with oxygen to form water:
Again, two reactants combine to form one product.
Carbon combines with oxygen to form carbon dioxide:

So, many substances combine to give one substance.
A decomposition reaction is a reaction in which one compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances. It is the opposite of a combination reaction.
Here, one reactant breaks down to form two or more products.
On heating calcium carbonate, it decomposes into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide:
Water can be decomposed into hydrogen and oxygen by passing electricity through it:
So, in a decomposition reaction, one compound breaks down into simpler substances.
A displacement reaction is a reaction in which a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound.
Here, element \(A\) is more reactive than \(B\), so \(A\) displaces \(B\) from the compound \(BC\).
Zinc reacts with copper sulphate solution:

items: Zinc displaces copper from copper sulphate.
Zinc sulphate and copper are formed.

blocks.text: Iron displaces copper from copper sulphate:
\[\text{More reactive element + Compound} \longrightarrow \text{New compound + Less reactive element}\]
Remember: A displacement reaction involves the displacement of one element by another more reactive element.
A double displacement reaction is a reaction in which two compounds exchange their ions to form two new compounds.
Here, the ions of the two compounds exchange places.
When sodium sulphate reacts with barium chloride:

items: \(\ce{BaSO4}\) is an insoluble white solid called a precipitate.

blocks.text: Therefore, this reaction is also called a precipitation reaction.
The compounds exchange their ions during the reaction.
Oxidation and reduction are chemical processes that often occur together in a reaction.
Copper combines with oxygen, so copper is oxidised.
Oxygen is removed from copper oxide, so copper oxide is reduced.
When oxidation and reduction occur in the same reaction, the reaction is called a redox reaction. For example:

Oxidation = Addition of Oxygen
Reduction = Removal of Oxygen
And:
Oxidation + Reduction = Redox Reaction

notes.heading: 1.3 Effects of Oxidation Reactions in Everyday Life

blocks.text: Oxidation reactions do not occur only in laboratories. They also happen around us in everyday life. Two important effects of oxidation are:
These processes can cause damage to metals and food.
Corrosion is the process in which a metal is gradually destroyed or damaged due to reactions with substances present in the environment, such as oxygen, moisture, acids, etc.
Iron reacts with oxygen and moisture present in air to form rust.
The reddish-brown coating seen on iron objects is rust.

items: Copper develops a green coating of basic copper carbonate.
Silver develops a black coating of silver sulphide.

blocks.text:
Corrosion can be prevented by protecting the metal from contact with air and moisture.
Common methods include:

Corrosion = Gradual damage of a metal due to environmental reactions
Rusting of iron is one of the most common examples of corrosion.
Rancidity is the process in which food containing fats and oils gets oxidised, causing an unpleasant smell and taste.
For example, when oily food is left exposed to air for a long time, it may develop a bad smell and taste. This happens because the fats and oils in the food undergo oxidation.
Rancidity can be prevented or slowed down by:

items: Keeping food in airtight containers to prevent contact with oxygen.
Packing some foods using nitrogen gas instead of oxygen.

blocks.text: Chips packets are often filled with nitrogen gas. Nitrogen prevents the oils in the chips from coming into contact with oxygen and becoming rancid.
Rancidity = Oxidation of fats and oils causing unpleasant smell and taste

summary: The chapter explains chemical reactions, chemical equations, balancing of equations, types of chemical reactions, oxidation and reduction, redox reactions, and the effects of oxidation in everyday life such as corrosion and rancidity.

qa.a: A chemical reaction is a process in which one or more substances change into new substances with different properties.
A chemical equation is a short representation of a chemical reaction using the symbols and chemical formulae of the substances involved.

qa.q: What is a skeletal chemical equation?
qa.a: A skeletal chemical equation represents a reaction but is not balanced.

qa.q: What is a balanced chemical equation?
qa.a: A balanced chemical equation is an equation in which the number of atoms of each element is equal on both sides of the equation.
A combination reaction is a reaction in which two or more substances combine to form a single product.
A decomposition reaction is a reaction in which one compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
A displacement reaction is a reaction in which a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound.

qa.q: What is a double displacement reaction?
qa.a: A double displacement reaction is a reaction in which two compounds exchange their ions to form two new compounds.
Oxidation can be understood as addition of oxygen, removal of hydrogen, or loss of electrons.
Reduction can be understood as removal of oxygen, addition of hydrogen, or gain of electrons.
When oxidation and reduction occur in the same reaction, the reaction is called a redox reaction.
